# Inspection evidence

Hash input bytes before and after review. Render in a separate temporary directory. Do not run macros, embedded code, or external links from a document. A DOCX is a ZIP: inspect word/document.xml (m:oMath, tables, paragraphs, field codes), relationships, and media, including SVG and raster fallback. Retain counts as inventory, not correctness claims. Compare actual embedded assets to the rendered pages and their captions; decorative logos are not scientific diagrams.

Use available LibreOffice/Pandoc or a trusted DOCX rendering tool, then open every page image. Record renderer and failures. For PDF, use a reader such as PyMuPDF/Poppler to render; inspect image pages even when text extraction is empty. Read full-resolution images where signs or labels are ambiguous. Rendering may differ in Word/Windows; disclose untested environments.

Inspect each submitted scientific drawing's provenance. Check original PNG RGBA values (visible pixels only) and background regions, SVG styles and included raster images, then final size on page. Flattened PDF color cannot establish original alpha. OCR is a reading aid, not authoritative transcription.

For structured JSON, read its supplied schema and manifest, preserve document bytes, use actual block IDs, and mark layout unavailable without exports. Never insert review fields in lecture content. Calculate only from explicit values; record exact fractions or symbolic derivation and scope conditions. Do not claim compilation or simulation from code reading.
